title: Reduced regular centers descend from etale closed models
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $T\subseteq |X|$ be closed, and let $M=T_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X$ be its reduced induced closed subscheme [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Suppose that for every $x\in T$ there are an etale morphism $e:W\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a point $w\in W$ with $e(w)=x$, and a regular reduced closed subscheme $C\hookrightarrow W$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] whose underlying subset is $e^{-1}(T)$. Then $M$ is regular. For every such chart, the pullback $M\times_XW$ [def-pc-fibre-product] equals $C$ as a closed subscheme of $W$, so their quasi-coherent defining ideal sheaves agree, and their local rings are canonically isomorphic at corresponding points. In particular, if $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $C=V(t_1,\ldots,t_c)$ is regular and reduced, where $t_1,\ldots,t_c\in A$ and $c\ge0$, the pulled-back ideal of $M$ is exactly $(t_1,\ldots,t_c)$, with no radical or further reduction. At a point of $C$ over $x$, the induced map from the local ring of $M$ at $x$ to the local ring of $C$ is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings [def-weil-flat-morphism]; its regular target witnesses regularity of the source. The ideal sheaf defining $M$ is locally finitely generated: on every Noetherian affine open it is the radical ideal of $T$ there. The assertions include $T=\varnothing$, for which $M$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 034E, lemma-reduced-local-smooth (reducedness under etale pullback); schemes.tex Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme (uniqueness of the reduced closed structure); algebra.tex Tag 00OF, lemma-flat-under-regular (descent on local rings). Applied in ILO VIII 4.1.8, printed p. 118.

proof.text: On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$, $R$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], $M\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ for the radical ideal $I$ of $T\cap U$, and its defining sheaf is $\widetilde I$. Every ideal of $R$ is finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], proving local finite generation of this sheaf. The algebra $R/I$ is of finite type over $R$ (with zero algebra generators), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. These affines cover $M$, so $M$ is locally Noetherian. For each $x\in M$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] describes $\mathcal O_{M,x}$ as a prime localization of one of these Noetherian quotient rings; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes this local ring Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme, affine construction; Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves; algebra.tex Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence

proof.text: Fix any chart $e:W\to X$ and $C\hookrightarrow W$ in the hypotheses, and put $P=M\times_XW$. The first assertion of [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent], applied with $Z=T$ and $D=M$, identifies $P$ with the reduced induced closed subscheme on $e^{-1}(T)$; its Cartier-divisor assertion is not used. Both $P$ and $C$ are therefore reduced closed subschemes with that same image. Apply uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] on $W$ to each: their ideal sheaves are the same vanishing ideal, and composing their unique isomorphisms to the reduced induced model gives a unique isomorphism $P\simeq C$ over $W$. This is equality as closed subschemes, independent of the chosen representatives of the fibre product. Taking germs of this isomorphism and its inverse gives mutually inverse local-ring maps at corresponding points of $P$ and $C$.

source.place: Tag 034E, lemma-reduced-local-smooth, as assembled in the first clause of lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent; schemes.tex Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme, uniqueness

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I$ be the ideal of $M$ in $X$. By [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image], the extended ideal $\operatorname{Im}(e^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_W)$ is precisely the defining ideal of $P\hookrightarrow W$. Step 2 identifies it with the defining ideal of $C$. If $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $C$ is cut out scheme-theoretically by $(t_1,\ldots,t_c)$, [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] identifies that defining ideal on $W$ with $(t_1,\ldots,t_c)$ itself. Consequently the pulled-back defining ideal is exactly this ideal. No radical is applied in this equality; reducedness was used in step 2 to identify the schemes. This includes $c=0$, where the ideal is zero and $C=W$.

source.place: Tag 01JU, lemma-fibre-product-immersion, part (1), ideal-image formula; Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme, uniqueness

proof.text: For each $x\in T$, choose a chart with $w\in W$ over $x$. Since $|C|=e^{-1}(T)$, $w$ corresponds to a point of $C$ and hence, by step 2, to a point $p\in P$ over the point of $M$ supported at $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], $P\to M$ is etale, being the base change of $e$. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] it is flat, and [def-weil-flat-morphism] says its stalk map $\mathcal O_{M,x}\to\mathcal O_{P,p}$ is a flat local homomorphism. Step 2 canonically identifies the target with $\mathcal O_{C,w}$. This target is a regular Noetherian local ring by the assumed regularity of $C$ and [def-weil-regular-scheme]; the source is Noetherian by step 1. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] applies and proves that $\mathcal O_{M,x}$ is regular. The same flat local-map assertion holds at every point of every supplied chart, by this identical base-change argument.

Step 1 gives local Noetherianity of $M$, and step 4 gives regularity of every one of its local rings. The equivalence in [def-weil-regular-scheme] therefore makes $M$ regular. If $T=\varnothing$, its reduced induced closed subscheme has empty underlying space by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; the local-ring conditions are vacuous, and step 1 still gives finite generation of the unit ideal defining the empty subscheme, and the preceding chart comparison identifies every $C$ and $P$ with the empty closed subscheme. Thus the empty case satisfies every assertion as well.
